_readme: HOW TO ADD A RELEASE: append ONE object to the top of `entries` (newest first), one block per release. Fields: id (unique slug, e.g. '2026-10-06-hardening'), date (YYYY-MM-DD), title, description, type (new | fixed | changed | breaking; the release headline type), tags (optional string[]), changes (optional sub-entries: [{ type, text }]). Nothing else needs editing: /changelog and the dashboard 'What's new' dot read this file. Keys starting with '_' are ignored.

entries.title: Availability: reliable schedules
entries.description: Schedules now work the way they should: date-specific rules no longer shift to the previous day, and the dashboard shows which schedule is actually active for each event type.

changes.text: Add date-specific schedule rules (e.g. a one-off block on a particular date) in the dashboard, alongside weekly rules.
Fixed a bug where date-specific availability rules could shift to the previous day depending on your location.
The availability and event-type pages now show which schedule is the active default for each event type.

entries.title: Booking analytics + conflict fix
entries.description: We added booking analytics to see how well the booking flow works for you, and fixed a rare case where a conflict on a very busy calendar could be missed.

changes.text: Booking analytics (self-hosted, no third parties) so we can measure booking success, time-to-book, and setup completion and prioritize fixes on real usage.
Fixed a rare case where a scheduling conflict could be missed when checking calendars with more than 250 events.

entries.title: 1.0 Hardening
entries.description: Our 1.0 hardening release: stricter CI, security fixes, and a tighter public API.

changes.text: New CI gates for typecheck, lint, and tests on every change.
Fixed a security issue where a Google calendar callback could be linked to another account.
The v1 API now requires tc_live_ API keys; raw user-id bearer tokens are no longer accepted.
Consolidated duplicated calendar client code into a single implementation.
